messages.author: 9cbdcb011f8600fa
messages.subject: Colorspace package and plotting errors
parts:
Hi all! 

Recently I tried playing with some color packages, but one of them would not install correctly, or load, and now I can't load anything related to plotting (e.g., ggplot2, effects, sjPlot, sjstats)... I am essentially at a stall now because I can't do anything. 
I tried removing and reinstalling packages directly from CRAN, removing and reinstalling R and RStudio, you name it, to no avail. The errors persist, always in the form of "Error: package or namespace load failed for ‘sjPlot’ in loadNamespace(i, c(lib.loc, .libPaths()), versionCheck = vI[[i]]):  there is no package called ‘colorspace’"

Nothing I do seems to affect this. 

Any suggestions? All the help forums just say to reinstall colorspace.... that does not work at all.  :(

messages.author: 27405c4b711a1080
messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: Colorspace package and plotting errors
parts:
Can you load colorspace on its own? 
library(colorspace)

If you can, can you provide your session_info()/sessionInfo()? 

How did you install colorspace?
Try installing from source instead of binary?

messages.author: d567d0ef3c054a35
messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: Colorspace package and plotting errors
parts:
The session_info() suggestion is a good idea.

This sounds to me as if there might be a mismatch between the current
version of R and the installed packages. E.g., in my local R
directory (i.e., *not* the systemwide directory) I currently have two
subdirectories:

$ ls
3.3 3.4

I'm running R version 3.4.2. I suspect that if I were to remove the
"3.4" subdirectory, I'd get complaints about packages not being
available for R 3.4.2. OTOH, this would be easily fixable by
re-installing the packages, so this may be a red herring.
